Batch: Windows AI, passkey, presence and security-control source recheck

Findings: Windows 11 version 24H2 provides per-app passkey consent in Settings.
Declining app consent prevents passkey registration and authentication for that app.
The page states that enterprise consent policies were targeted for general availability by the end of June 2026.
As checked 2026-10-25, base passkey access, per-app ForceAllow/ForceDeny/UserInControl lists, and passkey enumeration controls are still labeled Windows Insider Preview.
These policy nodes are device-scope; per-app list policies use semicolon-delimited Microsoft Store Package Family Names.
Presence-sensing app access and per-app controls are device-scope with a listed 10.0.25000+ build floor; this is not a named released Windows target.
The current page says Administrator protection is available with KB5120998, off by default, on Windows 11 Home, Pro, Enterprise and Education; Windows Server is not supported by the feature page.
A restart is required for enablement or disablement.
The current LocalPoliciesSecurityOptions CSP still labels the Administrator protection elevation-prompt policy Windows Insider Preview.
Settings transitions between Off and Enforcement are one-way unless the current mode is Evaluation.
The documented registry configuration is for testing and warns it could compromise protection.

LocalReadOnlyObservation.Finding: This local template contains the named passkey and human-presence policy entries. Host template presence is not Windows integration acceptance or evidence of a supported production target.

Resolved: Refreshed the selected controls' official source statements and documented current publication conflicts.
Deferred: Passkey enterprise policy implementation pending resolution of its passed general-availability target versus current Insider-only CSP labeling and per-app target acceptance.
Presence policy support pending a named released build and hardware/consumer verification.
Administrator protection policy backend pending reconciliation of feature availability with preview prompt-policy applicability.
Smart App Control state-changing operation pending a supported reversible path outside Evaluation.
MigrationDisposition.EstimateAdjustment: No legacy outcome closed; user-selected candidate controls remain separately tracked.
